summary: Require explicit write approval in the HTTP client (CLI --yes, never --agent; MCP write tools) and refuse identical FedEx writes that succeeded, are in flight, or ended with an unknown outcome in the last 24 hours.
reason: A timeout, agent retry, or double submit must not buy a second label or book a second pickup, and agent mode must not grant write authority. A self-confirmable preview/confirm round trip is not a human gate, so approval comes from --yes or the MCP client's per-call approval instead.
validated_outcome: Tests prove an unapproved write sends nothing, --agent does not imply --yes, generated write commands such as endofday close run with --yes, dry runs need no approval, identical writes (after canonicalizing key order and number spelling) are refused after success or an unknown outcome until --allow-duplicate / allow_duplicate, FedEx-rejected writes can be resent, a rejected forced resend keeps the earlier success or unknown outcome blocking, read-only POSTs are never gated, the ledger stores no request body and uses 0600 files, and stale locks are reclaimed.
